summary: Most high-contrast failures are placement errors: the prompt lets boundaries that force the model to finalize heads, titles, names, dates or agent nouns before the disambiguating head or explanatory phrase arrives. Rank/priority appears less important here (rank_lift is small); fixing segmentation decisions that prevent premature lexical commitment (especially around possessives 的, modifiers before heads, quoted meanings, parentheticals, and century/date phrases) should deliver the largest gain.

aggregate.dominant_basis: No corpus rate identifies a dominant failure. Read the cases and `judge_distribution` for WHICH mechanism to fix — do not infer a rate from `case_label_counts`, those cases were selected for being the worst.

coverage.of: all sentences scored — a true corpus rate
coverage.meaning: sentences where the tightest budget asked for boundaries the prompt never marked, so pieces are missing outright

premature_among_judged.of: boundaries judged this iteration, selected as the WORST by measured contradiction — NOT a corpus rate, do not compare it against `coverage`

case_label_counts.of: the selected worst cases — NOT a rate
